title: Warehouse Receiving Procedures
text: Warehouse Receiving Procedures. Inbound Scheduling. All inbound trucks must be scheduled through the dock appointment system at least 24 hours in advance. The receiving dock operates from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday. Carriers arriving without an appointment are worked in on a first-come, first-served basis only if dock capacity allows. Unloading and Inspection. Upon arrival, the driver checks in at the guard shack and proceeds to the assigned dock door. Warehouse staff unload pallets and verify the count against the bill of lading. Any visible damage is photographed and noted on the delivery receipt before the driver departs. Put-Away. After inspection, goods are labeled with license plate numbers and moved to their assigned storage locations within 4 hours of unloading. High-velocity SKUs are directed to forward pick locations near the packing stations. Discrepancies. Shortages, overages, or damaged goods are logged in the warehouse management system within 2 hours. The purchasing team is notified automatically for any variance above $500.

title: Inventory Management Policy
text: Inventory Management Policy. Safety Stock. Safety stock is calculated as average daily demand multiplied by the desired coverage in days, plus a variability buffer based on demand standard deviation. Standard coverage targets are 7 days for A-class SKUs, 14 days for B-class, and 21 days for C-class items. Reorder Points. The reorder point equals average daily demand times supplier lead time in days, plus safety stock. Purchase orders are triggered automatically when on-hand inventory falls to the reorder point. ABC Classification. SKUs are classified annually by revenue contribution: A items represent roughly 80 percent of revenue, B items 15 percent, and C items 5 percent. Classification drives counting frequency, safety stock targets, and review cadence. Obsolete Inventory. Inventory with no movement for 180 days is flagged for review. The planning team decides whether to discount, return to vendor, or write off the stock each quarter.

title: Freight Audit and Payment
text: Freight Audit and Payment. Invoice Auditing. Every freight invoice is matched against the original rate quote and the bill of lading before payment. An automated tolerance of 2% is allowed for minor accessorial charge differences; anything above 2% is flagged for manual review. Common Discrepancies. The most frequent discrepancies are duplicate fuel surcharges, incorrect weight breaks, and detention charges without supporting timestamps. Auditors must resolve flagged invoices within 5 business days. Payment Terms. Approved carrier invoices are paid on net-30 terms. Carriers enrolled in the quick-pay program receive payment in 7 days in exchange for a 1.5% discount. Carrier Scorecards. Carrier performance is scored monthly on on-time pickup, on-time delivery, invoice accuracy, and claims ratio. Carriers falling below 90% on-time delivery for two consecutive months are placed on probation.

title: Supplier Onboarding
text: Supplier Onboarding. Required Documentation. New suppliers must submit a completed W-9 (or W-8BEN for foreign entities), a certificate of insurance meeting our minimum coverage limits, banking details for ACH payments, and a signed supplier code of conduct. Qualification Process. The sourcing team evaluates suppliers on quality certifications (ISO 9001 preferred), financial stability, production capacity, and references from at least two existing customers. The full qualification process typically takes 3 to 4 weeks. System Setup. Once approved, the supplier record is created in the ERP system with payment terms, lead times, and approved ship-from locations. Suppliers gain access to the vendor portal for purchase orders, invoices, and shipment tracking. Performance Monitoring. New suppliers are reviewed after the first 90 days. Ongoing scorecards track defect rates, on-time delivery, and responsiveness. Suppliers must maintain a defect rate below 1% to retain preferred status.

title: Transportation Management System (TMS) Optimization
text: Transportation Management System (TMS) Optimization. Load Planning. The TMS consolidates less-than-truckload shipments into full truckloads whenever the combined volume exceeds 80% of trailer capacity. Optimized load plans are generated nightly for the next day's shipments. Carrier Selection. For each lane, the TMS ranks carriers by total cost, transit time reliability, and capacity commitment. The target on-time pickup rate across all carriers is 98%, and lanes falling below 95% trigger an automatic carrier review. Route Optimization. Dynamic routing considers traffic patterns, driver hours-of-service limits, and delivery appointment windows. Multi-stop routes are limited to 5 stops to protect on-time performance. Analytics. Weekly dashboards report cost per mile, cost per shipment, empty miles percentage, and tender acceptance rates. The logistics team reviews these metrics every Monday to identify savings opportunities.

title: Cold Chain Handling Procedures
text: Cold Chain Handling Procedures. Temperature Requirements. Refrigerated goods must be kept between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius throughout storage and transit. Frozen goods must remain at or below minus 18 degrees Celsius. Temperature is monitored continuously by calibrated sensors. Pre-Cooling. Trailers must be pre-cooled to the required temperature range before loading begins. Loading dock doors are kept closed except during active pallet transfer to minimize temperature excursions. Excursion Response. If a temperature excursion beyond the allowed range lasts more than 30 minutes, the shipment is quarantined and quality assurance is notified. QA determines whether the product can be released, downgraded, or destroyed. Documentation. Temperature logs accompany every cold chain shipment. Drivers record trailer temperature at pickup and delivery, and any excursion is documented with timestamps and corrective actions.

title: Returns and Reverse Logistics
text: Returns and Reverse Logistics. Return Window. Customers have 30 days from the delivery date to return unused items in their original packaging. Items returned after 30 days are accepted only with manager approval. Inspection and Grading. Returned items are inspected within 48 hours of arrival at the returns center. Products are graded as resellable, refurbishable, or scrap. Resellable items are restocked within 24 hours of grading. Refunds. Refunds are issued to the original payment method within 5 business days of the return being graded as resellable. Customers receive email notification when the refund is processed. Reverse Logistics Network. The company operates three regional returns centers. Carriers consolidate return shipments weekly to reduce transportation cost per unit.

title: Cycle Counting Procedures
text: Cycle Counting Procedures. Counting Frequency. A-class SKUs are cycle counted weekly, B-class SKUs monthly, and C-class SKUs quarterly. High-value items above $1,000 per unit are counted weekly regardless of ABC class. Blind Counts. Counters perform blind counts without seeing the system quantity. A second count is required if the first count differs from the system quantity by more than 1% or $100, whichever is greater. Reconciliation. Inventory control investigates and reconciles variances within 24 hours. Root causes such as misplaced pallets, unit-of-measure errors, or unrecorded shipments are documented for each adjustment. Accuracy Targets. The target inventory record accuracy is 98% for A-class SKUs and 95% overall. Facilities below target must submit a corrective action plan.

title: Last-Mile Delivery Operations
text: Last-Mile Delivery Operations. Delivery Promises. Orders in metro areas are eligible for same-day delivery if placed before 2:00 PM. Standard delivery promises are 2 business days for regional zones and 3 to 5 business days for remote zones. Driver Procedures. Drivers follow optimized route sequences from the dispatch app and capture proof of delivery with a photo and GPS timestamp. Failed deliveries are re-attempted the next business day; after two failed attempts the package is held at a pickup point. Customer Notifications. Customers receive SMS notifications at dispatch, when the driver is 5 stops away, and at delivery. Real-time tracking is available through the order status page. Performance Metrics. Key metrics include on-time delivery rate (target 97%), cost per stop, and first-attempt success rate. Routes are re-optimized monthly based on stop density changes.

title: Customs and Trade Compliance
text: Customs and Trade Compliance. Import Documentation. Every US import shipment requires CBP Form 7501 (Entry Summary), a commercial invoice, a packing list, and the bill of lading. The customs broker must receive documents at least 48 hours before vessel arrival. Duties and Classification. Products are classified under the Harmonized Tariff Schedule to determine duty rates. The trade compliance team reviews classifications annually and whenever a product design changes. Denied Party Screening. All customers, suppliers, and intermediaries are screened against denied party lists before any transaction. Matches are escalated to the compliance officer and the transaction is held. Record Keeping. Import and export records are retained for 5 years from the date of entry. The compliance team conducts quarterly self-audits of broker filings and duty payments.
